facts: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country, with over 200 million people.
Nigeria has more than 500 languages.
Lagos was Nigeria's capital until 1991, when Abuja took over.
flex: Nollywood is one of the largest film industries in the world by number of films produced.

facts: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence from colonial rule, in 1957.
Ghana is one of the world's biggest cocoa producers.
Lake Volta in Ghana is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world.
flex: Ghana's independence under Kwame Nkrumah helped inspire other African independence movements.

facts: South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein, each hosting a different arm of government.
South Africa has 11 official languages.
South Africa is the world's largest producer of platinum.
flex: South Africa was the first African country to host the FIFA World Cup, in 2010.

facts: Sudan has more pyramids than Egypt.
The Great Pyramid of Giza was built about 4,500 years ago.
The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, connects the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea.
flex: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest man-made structure in the world for roughly 3,800 years.

facts: M-Pesa, the mobile money service, launched in Kenya in 2007.
Kenya is famous for its long-distance runners, who have won many Olympic and marathon titles.
The Great Rift Valley runs through Kenya.
flex: In 2019, Kenya's Eliud Kipchoge ran a marathon in under two hours, though it was not an official record.

facts: Ethiopia uses a calendar with 13 months.
The Ethiopian calendar is about seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar.
Coffee is widely believed to have originated in Ethiopia.
flex: Ethiopia defeated Italy at the Battle of Adwa in 1896 and kept its independence.

facts: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa.
Lesotho is the only country in the world whose entire land is above 1,000 metres.
Lesotho is known as the Kingdom in the Sky.
flex: Lesotho is a proud kingdom with its own king, language and flag, independent since 1966.

facts: Morocco is home to al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859 and often called the oldest continuously operating university in the world.
Spain is only about 14 kilometres from Morocco across the Strait of Gibraltar.
Morocco has a famous blue city called Chefchaouen.
flex: Morocco reached the World Cup semi-finals in 2022, the first African team to do so.

facts: Jollof rice is widely traced back to the Wolof people of Senegal and the Gambia.
Dakar is the westernmost capital on the African mainland.

flex: Senegal won the Africa Cup of Nations in early 2022.

facts: Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania is the highest mountain in Africa.
The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 is often called the shortest war in history, lasting about 40 minutes.
Tanzania was formed in 1964 when Tanganyika and Zanzibar united.
flex: Tanzania is home to the Serengeti, famous for its great wildebeest migration.
